opportunity.title: Brand Name or Equal: Qgenda Scheduling Software (Sources Sought)
opportunity.description: Sources Sought for Qgenda scheduling software, brand name or equal, issued by Network Contract Office 19. Information and planning only, not a solicitation. Responses limited to 8 pages, due by email Oct 23, 2026 at 15:00 MST; proprietary information should be marked. VA identified NAICS 541519 Other Computer Related Services with a $34 million size standard and asks respondents to say if a different NAICS fits better. Interested contractors submit an overview of the proposed solution and a capability or qualifications statement.

rationale.point: Atlas Federal is a large IT services contractor with NAICS 541519 alignment and direct health IT experience (Defense Health Agency data program), positioning it to provide integration, implementation, and support services for scheduling software.

The VA's prior $93,536 award for Qgenda licenses was small, but the Sources Sought under NAICS 541519 has a median top award near $99.5M, indicating potential for a substantial follow-on services contract that fits Atlas's $5M–$60M prime contract range.

The identified competitors (PerfectServe Lightning Bolt, M7 Health, ShiftRx, DataSpring) show a competitive COTS scheduling market; Atlas could partner with Qgenda or an alternative vendor to deliver a complete solution.
No set-aside applies and Atlas meets all eligibility gates (deadline, NAICS, place of performance), so there is no socioeconomic barrier to participation.

risks: The acquisition may be limited to COTS license procurement only, with no services component, reducing Atlas's value proposition.
Brand-name-or-equal language may favor incumbent Qgenda resellers; Atlas lacks a known reseller agreement with Qgenda or the listed competitors.
Responding to a Sources Sought does not guarantee a subsequent solicitation or that the requirement will be structured for a large prime contractor.
nextSteps: Confirm whether Atlas has or can quickly establish a teaming arrangement with Qgenda or a competitor (PerfectServe, M7 Health, ShiftRx, DataSpring).
Engage the VA contracting office to clarify if the anticipated solicitation includes implementation, integration, training, and sustainment services.
Monitor for the formal solicitation and reassess bid/no-bid once the scope, evaluation criteria, and contract vehicle are known.
